 JUDGMENT

The petitioners in both the petitions have filed their respective petitions under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries sustained by them in a Road Traffic Accident.
To avoid conflicting Judgments, they are clubbed together and are taken together for common disposal.

The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
On 24.09.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner in MVC No.980/2023 was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JP-9008 along with petitioner in MVC No.979/2023 as a pillion rider near Nelamangala- Kunigal, NH-75 road, near Lanco Toll, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru.
At that time one Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MG-0186 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle.
Due to the impact of the said accident, both petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body.

Immediately, the petitioner in MVC No.979/2023 was taken to Government Hospital,
Nelamangala and then shifted to Shreyas Hospital wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he was discharged with an advice for continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest.
4. Like wise, the petitioner in MVC No.980/2023 was taken to Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru and then shifted to Government Hospital, Nelamangala wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he was discharged with an advice for continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest.

6. The petitioner in MVC No.979/2023, she was hale and healthy and was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident.
She was working as a Factory worker and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
She was maintaining her family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to her family.
Due to the accidental injuries she could not able to do any kind of work compared to her previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on her earning capacity and as such herself and her family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
7. The petitioner in MVC No.980/2023, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 30 years as on the date of accident.
He was working as a Factory worker and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
8. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent drive of the respondent No.1, who drove his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MG-0186.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said vehicle
thereby the vicarious liability is operated on respondent No.2 on the indemnified contract and as such, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
9. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the vehicle involved in the accident, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- each together with 980/2023 interest and cost from the date of petition till realization.
Hence, prayed to allow the petitions.
10. After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.

In pursuance of service of notice the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and the respondent No.1 has not filed the written statement, therefore the written statement of the respondent No.1 is taken has not filed.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement on behalf of respondent No.2 by denying the entire petition averments.
The respondent No.2 further pleaded that the insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied the age of the petitioner, avocation, income,
injuries sustained, treatment underwent by the petitioner, disability certificate obtained by the petitioner, medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment of the said petitioner.
Further denied the other contents of the 980/2023 petition.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

ISSUE NO.2 IN MVC No.979/2023:

The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.

1. Pecuniary loss:- This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous 980/2023 expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.

(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-
In order to determine the compensation under this head, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate which are marked as per Ex.P.8.
As per the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
The Ex.P.10 is the discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to hospital from 24.09.2022 to 29.09.2022 for a period of 6 days.
These documents shows that petitioners have taken treatment in Shreyas Hospital, Bengaluru, but the 980/2023 doctor is not examined by petitioner.
Without the examination of the doctor it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained any injuries.

These documents shows that petitioners have taken treatment in Shreyas Hospital, Bangalore.
Without the evidence of doctor towards assessment of disability it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained any injuries.

In number of Judgments delivered by the Hon'ble Apex Court it is highlighted that 980/2023 i) In a motor vehicle accident case, where a doctor was not examined court may award "global compensation" which is typically a lower amount due to the lack of concrete medical evidence to support the extent of injuries often resulting in a reduced compensation package compared to cases with proper medical documentation.
Due to lack of crucial medical evidence from the doctors only covers minimal damages or pain and sufferings.

ii). Courts may reason that without a proper medical examination, it is difficult to accurately assess the extent of the disability and the resulting loss of income or future prospectus leading to a lower over all compensation award.
iii). Even if a doctor was not examined, the court may still consider the visible injuries or the severity of the accident when determining the compensation amount.
The court may rely on the claimant's own testimony regarding their injuries and limitations but this may be less persuasive without supporting medical evidence.

v). Some cases has seen tribunals award a nominal compensation amount such as a few thousand rupees, when a claimant failed to present a doctor's examination report, highlighting the importance of medical documentation in such cases.
vi) Not examining the doctor significantly weakens the plaintiff's case as it make it difficulty to establish the standard of care that was breached and the patient's injury.
vii) The plaintiff bears the burden of proving medical negligence and failing to examine the treating doctor can make it challenging to meet this standard.

980/2023 viii) Several Indian Court cases have highlighted the issue of not examining the treating doctor,
resulting in significantly reduced compensation awards.
ix) Even if a court does award compensation, the amount will likely be lower due to factors like the severity of the injury, availability of other medical evidence and the plaintiff's contribution to the situation.

(a) Pain and sufferings and mental agony:-
According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained injuries as on the date of accident.
